OneOS will run \"su -c id\" once. It only prints which user it runs as and changes nothing.\n\nMagisk may ask you to allow OneOS. In KernelSU or APatch, allow OneOS in the superuser list first.

Reads facts about this phone as root: build properties, CPU features, One UI\'s installd interface, displays, touch, backlight, services, SELinux policy, storage and root manager. The OneOS team checks the findings before any build that can switch is shared.

Every command only reads. Root writes no file, sets no property or setting and starts or stops nothing. The results go to OneOS over a pipe and stay in its own storage until you share them. Tap a test below to see its exact command.

Before anything can be shared, OneOS removes IMEI and MEID, serial numbers and device IDs, MAC addresses, SIM numbers (ICCID, IMSI), phone numbers, emails, Wi-Fi names, account names and locations. No logs, messages, contacts, photos or files are read. You can open every file before sharing.
